sentences.text:
The case of prosecution in brief is that on 29.10.2022 at about 08.30 PM, near Road No. 13,
Kalindi Kunj to Okhla, in front of Living Style Mall, within the jurisdiction of PS Sarita Vihar, the State vs Dinesh on 10 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/56002567/
1

Accused Dinesh was driving one motorcycle bearing registration no. HR 51 BR 9056, in a rash and negligent manner, so as to endanger human life and personal safety of others and while so driving Accused person has hit a child namely Rudra Tanwar and caused simple injury to him.
As such, it is alleged that the Accused person has committed the offences punishable under section 279/337 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 (hereinafter, "IPC").
It is in relation of these offences, for which the present FIR was lodged in PS Sarita Vihar.
2. After registration of the case, necessary investigation was carried out by the IO concerned.
Site plan was prepared.
Statement of witnesses were recorded under section 161 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 (hereinafter, "CrPC").
Relevant record was collected.
Final report under section 173 CrPC, was prepared against the abovenamed Accused person and chalan was presented in the court on 12.01.2023.
After taking cognizance of the offence, the Accused person was summoned to face trial vide order dated 12.01.2023.
3. On his appearance, a copy of chargesheet was supplied to him in terms of section 207 of CrPC.
On finding a prima facie case against the Accused person, notice under section 279/337 IPC was served upon the Accused person on 24.03.2023.
The Accused person pleaded not guilty and claimed trial.
Thereafter, the complainant gave his statement that the offence u/s 337 IPC had been settled with the Accused upon payment of compensation of Rs. 5000.
Compensation was paid and statement of the complainant was recorded and the Accused was acquitted of the offence punishable u/s 337 IPC.
PROSECUTION EVIDENCE 4.

During the trial for the offence u/s 279 IPC, prosecution led the following oral and documentary evidence against the Accused to prove its case beyond reasonable doubt: -
ORAL EVIDENCE PW1 :- Pooja W/o Arun (Complainant/Mother of Injured child in the present case)
DOCUMENTARY EVIDENCE
Ex. PW1
/ A :- Written complaint of the complainant
. Ex. PW1
/ B :- Seizure memo of the offending vehicle

Ex. PW1/C :-
Seizure memo of the documents of the offending vehicle
Ex. PW1/D :- Arrest memo of the Accused
Ex. PW1/
E :- Personal search memo of the Accused
Ex. A1, Ex
. :- FIR No. 518/2022, endorsement on rukka A2 and Ex. and certificate u/s 65B Indian Evidence A3 Act.
Ex. A4 :- Mechanical Inspection Report dt.
Ex. A6 :- Insurance certificate in respect of the  offending vehicle.

Ex. A7 :- Notice u/s 133 MV Act issued to State vs Dinesh on 10 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/56002567/
2  registered owner of offending vehicle.
Ex. A8 :- Seizure memo of the offending vehicle Ex. A9 and :- Arrest memo and personal search memo of Ex. A 10 the Accused.

Ex. A11 and :- GD No. 71A and 70A.
Ex. A12 5.

During the course of trial, witnesses mentioned at Sr. No. 2, 3 and 4 of the list of witnesses, were dropped pursuant to statement of the Accused recorded u/s 294 CrPC.
6.

Thereafter, PW-1, i.e., the complainant was examined, who turned hostile, even on the point of identity of the driver, identity of the offending vehicle and the manner in which the said offending vehicle was being driven.
The said witness, who was the only public witness/eye witness was cross examined by Ld. APP, with permission of the court.
However, nothing incriminating was brought on record in the said cross examination.

7. Rest of the prosecution witnesses were only official witnesses, such as the arrest witness and the IO, whose testimony even if taken together, would not have been sufficient to prove the allegations against the Accused.
Accordingly, further recording of prosecution evidence was stopped to prevent unnecessary delay and wastage of state expenses.

Hence, vide order dated 19.10.2023, recording of further prosecution evidence was stopped, as in the present case, the same would have resulted in to wastage of judicial time, money, resources and will also cause unnecessary oppression to the Accused person.

In this regard reference may be made to a Division Bench Judgement of the Hon'ble High Court of Delhi passed in the case of Govind &
Ors. vs. The State (Govt. of NCT of Delhi) 104 (2003) DLT 510 wherein it was held that: -
"...In cases where the ultimate chance of conviction is very bleak for there is no prospect of the case and again conviction in such cases no useful purpose is likely to be served by allowing a criminal prosecution and trial to continue.

Govind &
Ors. vs. The State (Govt. of NCT of Delhi) 104 (2003) DLT 510
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is advisable to truncate or snip the proceedings and save valuable time of the courts.

The trial should not be continued only for the purpose of formally completing the proceedings to pronounce the conclusion of a future date."
8.
Right to speedy trial is constitutionally guaranteed fundamental right of the Accused person.

The present case pertains to an FIR of the year 2022 and continuing the trial any further, when it is clear that prosecution can never hope to prove its case against the Accused person would tantamount to State vs Dinesh on 10 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/56002567/
3 violation of right to speedy trial of the Accused person.

It has been held in P.Ramchandra Rao vs.
State of Karnataka AIR 2022 SC 1856 that the court should exercise its power available under Criminal Procedure Code to give effect to the right of speedy trial to the Accused.

P.Ramchandra Rao vs.
State of Karnataka AIR 2022 SC 1856
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Similar observations were made in Pankaj Kumar vs. State of Mahrashtra AIR 2008 SC 3057.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

Furthermore,
in Satish Mehra vs. Delhi Administration & Abr. 1996 JCC 507 Hon'ble Supreme Court has held that valuable time of the court should not be wasted merely for formal completion of procedure when there is no chance of the trial culminating in conviction.

sentences.text: STATEMENT OF ACCUSED 9.
Since there was no incriminating evidence on record against the Accused person, the statement of the Accused u/s 313 CrPC was dispensed with.
ARGUMENTS AND ANALYSIS 10.
I have heard the Ld. APP for the state and Ld. counsel for the Accused at length.
I have also given my thoughtful consideration to the material appearing on record.
11. It is argued by the Ld. APP for the state that there is sufficient material on record to convict the Accused for the said offences.
12. Per contra, the Ld. counsel for the Accused has argued that the state has failed to establish its case beyond reasonable doubt.
Ld. Counsel has argued that main prosecution witness has failed to identify the Accused, the offending vehicle and has not even deposed as to the way in which the offending vehicle was being driven.
Hence, nothing has come on record against the Accused.
As such, it is prayed that the Accused person be acquitted for the said offences.
13. The Accused person has been charged for the offence under section 279/337 IPC.
The Accused has already been acquitted of the offence punishable u/s 337 IPC vide order dated 19.10.2023 on account of settlement/compounding.
The presumption of innocence of the Accused has to be rebutted by the prosecution by reducing cogent evidence that points towards the guilt of the Accused.
The evidence in the present case is to be weighed keeping in view the above legal standards.

15. The main witness of the prosecution, namely PW Pooja, who was the only eye witness to the incident has stated that she does not remember the registration number of the offending vehicle and has refused to identify the driver of the offending vehicle.

It has been stated by her that she has not State vs Dinesh on 10 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/56002567/
4 seen the driver at the time of the incident.
Hence, no averment as to the Accused driving the offending vehicle or the offending vehicle being driven in a rash and negligent manner has been made by her.

In fact, in the cross examination conducted by Ld. APP for the state, a suggestion was put to the witnesses that the offending vehicle was being driven in a rash and negligent manner,
which she denied.
Thus, there is nothing to implicate the Accused person in the present case.
As such, even if all the other prosecution witness cited in the list of witnesses were to be examined, the case of the prosecution could not be proved.

16. Furthermore, it has been held by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Dr. S.L. Goswami vs. State of Madhya Pradesh 197 SCC (Crl.) 258 that the Accused persons are entitled to benefit of doubt where the onus of proving the ingredients of the offence is not discharged by the prosecution.

entities.text: Dr. S.L. Goswami vs. State of Madhya Pradesh 197 SCC (Crl.) 258
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 17. To recapitulate the above discussion, to bring home the guilt of Accused person, the prosecution was required to prove the offence under section 279 IPC beyond reasonable doubt.
The star witness of the prosecution i.e., the eye witness, PW1 has turned hostile.
There is no evidence to link the Accused person with the crime charged against him.
His driving the vehicle in a rash and negligent manner is not proved during the trial.
Further, the ingredients of the offence are not fulfilled from the material on record.

In the present case, as already noted above, the prosecution could not discharge the onus of proving the ingredients of offences in question and thus, the Accused person is entitled to benefit of doubt.
18. Resultantly, the Accused person namely, DINESH S/o CHOKHE LAL is hereby found not guilty.
He is hereby ACQUITTED of the offence under section 279 IPC.
Announced in open court on 10.11.2023 in the presence of the Accused.
